script.text: Oil is above 100 dollars. U.S. borrowing costs are near a 24-year high. Linked?

Brent crude traded around 104 dollars on Monday, Bloomberg reports, after Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia over the weekend. Market Index says attacks on shipping and Saudi targets keep Brent anchored above 100 dollars.

Why does that reach bonds? Costlier oil can push up inflation, and lenders then ask for more. CNBC and Bloomberg report the ten-year Treasury yield rose above 5 percent last week, the highest since 2002.

Now two tests arrive. JPMorgan reports earnings on Tuesday. On Wednesday, September inflation data is due. Forecasts point to 3.6 percent, up from 3.4, according to market previews. The S and P 500 still closed Friday near its record. A hot reading could revive talk of Fed rate hikes, CNBC notes.
Will this week's inflation data push yields higher? Yes or no?
